figures.caption: (a) Chemical structure of Spiniferin. (b) Cytotoxicity studies of Spiniferin, its new analogs, and Temporin L (a well-studied membrane-active cytotoxic AMP) by determining viability of mouse macrophage RAW 264.7 cells. (c) Hemolysis of hRBCs in the presence of the peptides, as marked in the figure. (d) In vivo toxicity of Spiniferin­(E4dR) at different doses in BALB/c mice in the intravenous route. (e) Results of serum protease stability assays of Spiniferin­(E4R) and Spiniferin­(E4dR) by RP-HPLC in 10% human serum.
Time-Killing kinetic assay. (a) S. aureus ATCC 25923, (b) MRSA ATCC 33591, and (c) E. coli ATCC 25922. (d) Minimum bactericidal concentration of Spiniferin­(E4dR) against the selected bacteria.

Phospholipid membrane interaction of Spiniferin-derived peptides. Tryptophan fluorescence spectra of these peptides: (a) in the presence of PC:PG (3:1, w/w) lipid vesicles and (b) in the presence of PC:Chol (8:1, w/w). Quenching of tryptophan fluorescence values in the presence of different concentrations of acrylamide at 340 nm of Spiniferin, Spiniferin­(E4R), Spiniferin­(E4dR), and Spiniferin­(E4dK) in the presence of PC:PG lipid vesicles (c) and PC:Chol lipid vesicles. (d) The concentration of quencher was varied between 10 and 100 mM in both kinds of lipid vesicles. Panel (e) shows the tryptophan emission maxima shifts of Spinifirin, Spiniferin­(E4R), Spiniferin­(E4dR), and Spiniferin­(E4dK) toward shorter wavelengths in the presence of PC:PG and PC:Chol lipid vesicles.

Secondary structure estimation of Spiniferin, Spiniferin­(E4R), and Spiniferin­(E4dR) in the presence of bacterial and mammalian membrane-mimetic lipid vesicles. (a) CD spectra of the peptides in the presence of different lipid vesicles, (b) percentage of secondary structures of these peptides (α-helix, β-sheet) in PC:PG and PC:Chol [Peptide (50 μM), PC:PG (0.624 mM), PC:Chol (0.408 mM)]. (c) β-strand projection of Spiniferin, Spiniferin­(E4R), Spiniferin­(E4dR).

Computational modeling of Spiniferin­(E4R) and Spiniferin­(E4dR) after 100 ns molecular dynamic simulation of each of these peptides. Distances between the cationic sites of arginine residues and aromatic carbon atoms of tryptophan residues are shown in both the peptides.

Peptide-induced depolarization of different bacteria and hRBCs (a). Peptides, bacteria, and hRBCs are marked in different panels of the figure. (b) Plots of % fluorescence recovery of dis-C3–5 fluorescence as a result of dissipation of diffusion potential across these cellular membranes in the presence of different concentrations of the peptides. Assessment of peptide-induced SYTOX-Green uptake in different bacteria. (c) Peptides and bacteria are shown in panel (c). (d) The extent of SYTOX-green uptake shown in terms of fluorescence recovery with different concentrations of the peptides.

Visualization of different peptide-induced damage on the membrane organization and morphology of the selected bacteria. Scanning electron microscopy: (a) E. coli ATCC 25922 control, bacteria without any treatment, bacteria after treatment with Temporin L, Spiniferin, and Spiniferin­(E4dR) at 5× MIC for 2 h. (b) S. aureus ATCC 25923 untreated bacteria and the same bacteria after treatment with Temporin L, Spiniferin, and Spiniferin­(E4dR) at 5× MIC.

Effect of Spiniferin­(E4dR) peptide on the survival of E. coli-infected BALB/c mice. (a) E. coli ATCC 25922 (2 × 107 CFU/mL)-infected BALB/c mice were treated with a single dose of Spiniferin­(E4dR) (6 and 12 mg/kg) injected through the intravenous route. A group of mice treated with ciprofloxacin (10 mg/kg) served as a positive control and E. coli-infected mice without any peptide/antibiotic treatment served as a negative control and were observed for 7 days after treatment. (b) Bacterial CFU counting assays were performed with visceral organs of E. coli-infected BALB/c mice under different conditions. E. coli injected into mice through i.p. route, post 1 h of infection, Spiniferin­(E4dR) (12 mg/kg) injected intravenously. Mice treated with ciprofloxacin (10 mg/kg) were used as the positive control, and mice infected only with bacteria and no treatment of peptide/antibiotic were used as the control. Statistical analysis was done by using two-way ANOVA Dunnett’s multiple comparisons test, **p = 0.0031, ***p = 0.0001, ****p < 0.0001.
